about: A machine check names the processor by APIC id. With a measured map (apic id to logical processor) the core is exact; without one the id is taken as the logical processor's number. An id nobody owns blames no core. 'cores' lists physical cores: {count, threadsPerCore} means core N owns logical processors N*t .. N*t+t-1. 'map' is null (no map), {identity: n} (apic id = logical processor, n of them) or {pairs: [[apic, logical], ...]}.

cases.name: without a map the old assumption holds on the verified part (apic 9 is core 4)
without a map apic 0 is core 0
an identity map gives the same answer as no map (apic 9)
an identity map gives the same answer as no map (apic 15)
a gap in the ids: the old rule credits apic 16 to core 8
a gap in the ids: the measured map says apic 16 is core 6
both siblings of a core resolve to it (apic 17)
an id in the gap belongs to no processor so it blames no core
an id outside every core blames no core
